reasons.hook: Eight words, self-explanatory, and the second person makes the viewer the mechanism. Docked one because 'every play' takes a beat to register as impossible.
reasons.retention: Clean escalation from eleven plays to four hundred, and the frame counter gives the middle something to watch. The 0:17-0:23 time-lapse is the softest stretch.
reasons.originality: Heavily docked. The central mechanism - it advances only while somebody watches - is the same engine as 004 in this same batch. It is also not the source concept's mechanism: PIX-002's twist is that the appended frames are continuous real time. The script drifted into another script's idea.
reasons.twist: The reversal genuinely reframes the file from object to process, and the handover to the viewer is a strong comment driver.
reasons.visual: Progress bars and an empty room. Legible but screen-dominant; only three shots have real depth.
reasons.clarity: No ambiguity anywhere. Every line is a single fact.
reasons.resembles_another: Shares its central mechanism with 004 (One Step Closer). Two of the first ten Shorts would teach the audience the same rule.

rounds.notes: Rejected on mechanism overlap with 004, not on score. Rewrite must restore PIX-002's own twist and leave the observation mechanic to 004.

triggers.resembles_another: reviewer: Shares its central mechanism with 004 (One Step Closer). Two of the first ten Shorts would teach the audience the same rule.

reasons.hook: Unchanged and still the second strongest in the batch.
reasons.retention: Unchanged. The 2003 line gives the middle a concrete anchor it did not have before.
reasons.originality: Resolved. The observation mechanic is gone and the script now runs on its own concept's twist - continuous real time - which no other script in the batch uses. The collision with 004 no longer exists.
reasons.twist: Slightly different in kind and equally strong: the reveal is now temporal rather than participatory. Twenty-two years of a room, played back one frame at a time, reframes the empty footage retroactively.
reasons.clarity: Unchanged. Every line is one fact.

rounds.notes: Approved. The rewrite also brought the script back in line with the concept it was commissioned from.
rounds.rewrite_note: Removed the 'it only moves while somebody is watching' mechanism, which duplicated 004 and was not in the source concept. Replaced it with PIX-002's own twist: the appended frames are continuous real time and the camera never stopped. Final two lines and two captions rewritten to match.

reasons.hook: An absence and a contradiction in eight words. Two points down only because 'the room' has to be established as a place rather than a thing.
reasons.retention: Every beat adds a fact: the camera number, the count, the missing lens, the angle. Nothing repeats.
reasons.originality: Recursion is a known shape, but the route in - a file with a camera ID that does not exist - is specific, and the eleventh-layer ending is not the usual infinite-mirror gag.
reasons.twist: Full marks. The recursion is not a display error, it is eleven real vantage points, and the empty chair inverts the whole video.
reasons.visual: Best-shot construction in the batch. Monitors inside monitors need zero narration.
reasons.clarity: Every step is procedural and followable.

rounds.notes: Strongest script in the batch. Approved without changes.

reasons.hook: Arithmetic. Nine words, no technical knowledge, and the viewer spots the impossibility themselves.
reasons.retention: The measuring beat and the travel log are both active investigation. The nine-years line at 0:12 is the one place the script pauses to tell rather than show.
reasons.originality: A sealed room behind a wall is well-trodden ground. What earns the score is the route in - a cleaning log filling in for a room nobody can reach - rather than the destination.
reasons.twist: Docked. By the time the travel log appears, most viewers have predicted a hidden room. The payoff is the clean floor, not the room, and the script arrives there a beat late.
reasons.visual: A vector floor plan, a torch, plaster dust and a spotless floor. Immediately readable at phone size.

rounds.notes: Approved. The twist is anticipated rather than surprising, but the final image carries it.

reasons.hook: Seven words containing a cause and an effect. The best hook line in the batch.
reasons.retention: The week of leaving it alone is a genuine structural risk that pays off - it converts the viewer's own instinct into the escalation.
reasons.originality: Docked for sharing its observation mechanic with 001. This script owns the idea; 001 is the one being rewritten, but two scripts reaching for the same rule in one batch is a batch-level failure.
reasons.twist: 'It is not the deleting, it is the attention' is a real category flip rather than an escalation.
reasons.visual: Phone screen and one hallway. Strong final image, thin middle.

rounds.notes: Approved. Originality docked for a batch-level collision that 001 is being rewritten to resolve.

reasons.hook: Six words. The shortest complete impossibility in the batch and the fastest to read.
reasons.retention: The chair test at 0:07 is the strongest mid-video beat in the set - the character proves the anomaly on camera instead of describing it.
reasons.originality: Precognitive footage is common; a second camera sealed in the wall pointed at the first is not, and it converts the premise from prophecy to surveillance.
reasons.twist: Strong category flip. Docked one because the wall-opening is telegraphed by the angle discussion thirty seconds earlier.
reasons.visual: Institutional corridors and a dust-covered lens in a cavity. Good, not spectacular.
reasons.clarity: The angle explanation is the only place a viewer might need a second pass, and the diagram shot covers it.

failed_checks: twist: twist line introduces at least two new terms

reasons.hook: Nine words, an ordinary action against an impossible result. Docked three because 'the conversation' has no antecedent yet, so the first beat is slightly abstract.
reasons.retention: The 1999 and 2003 lines are the turn, and they arrive on time. The scroll sequences risk feeling like texture rather than progress.
reasons.originality: Old hardware still connected is familiar; the inversion that the modern life is the echo is not.
reasons.twist: Full marks. It reverses the direction of the entire story rather than adding to it.
reasons.visual: CRT phosphor and a loft. Atmospheric but text-heavy, and text is the hardest thing to read on a phone.
reasons.clarity: Docked. 'He is three seconds behind' requires the viewer to hold two timelines at once, and at 0:45 there is no room left to help them.

rounds.notes: Approved. Clarity is the weak dimension; the sound design carries the final beat and must land.

reasons.hook: A quantity and a contradiction. Docked two because 'two hundred hours' needs a half-beat to feel large.
reasons.retention: The drive is the weakest stretch - it is transit rather than investigation - but the rental form and the key recover it.
reasons.originality: Location-history anomalies are a known seed; the storage unit full of identical phones is specific enough to own.
reasons.twist: Docked. The unit is a spectacle rather than a reversal. Nothing the viewer believed at 0:20 is overturned; the scale simply increases.
reasons.visual: The single most arresting final image in the batch.

rounds.notes: Approved. Twist is the weak dimension and is worth watching in the retention data.

reasons.hook: Nine words that trust the audience to know a 1998 living room. Docked two because it needs the viewer to picture the era.
reasons.retention: Confirms the automated finding. Between 0:13 and 0:25 the captions introduce nothing new - 'He zooms in' and 'The screen is on' are the same beat twice, and twelve seconds is a long time to ask a viewer to wait.
reasons.originality: An anachronism in old footage is a known device, but pointing it at the viewer's own room is a specific and well-earned turn.
reasons.twist: The screen showing the room the tape is being watched in is a genuine observer inversion.
reasons.visual: Two clearly separated visual worlds, which is the strongest look in the batch.

rounds.notes: Rejected on the twelve-second dead patch and an early twist beat, both confirmed on reading. Score would otherwise have passed, which is the point of the triggers.

triggers.dead_air: reviewer: confirms the automated finding - between 0:13 and 0:25 the captions introduce nothing new, and twelve seconds is a long time to ask a viewer to wait.

reasons.retention: Resolved. The longest stretch without new on-screen information is now under eight seconds, and the added line at 0:13 gives the zoom sequence a reason to exist beyond waiting.
reasons.twist: Unchanged in substance and better placed. The beat now falls at 50% of the voiceover instead of 40%, so the escalation has somewhere to go.
reasons.visual: Unchanged. Still the strongest look in the batch.

suspected.weak_ending: closing pair introduces no new terms

overrides.weak_ending: Flagged because the closing pair introduces no new vocabulary. Overridden: the repetition is the device. 'All of them looking at the screen / All of them looking at him' turns on the swapped object, and any new word in that position would break the anaphora. The lexical novelty test cannot see a rhetorical turn.

rounds.rewrite_note: Rewrote the 0:13-0:25 stretch so every caption introduces new information, moved the twist beat from 40% to 50% of the voiceover, and replaced the duplicated 'screen is on' beat with a line that advances the reveal.

reasons.hook: Nine words and the violation is understood instantly in any market.
reasons.retention: The purchase and the wait are good structure. The seller-profile beat at 0:08 is the softest.
reasons.originality: A listing photographed inside the buyer's own home is a genuinely fresh seed, and the substitution reading is not the obvious one.
reasons.twist: Docked. The final line is a scope statement rather than an image, and 'none of the buyers are her' asks the viewer to do arithmetic at the exact moment they should be feeling something.
reasons.visual: Warm domestic against clinical product photography. Two lamps side by side is an excellent single frame.
reasons.clarity: Docked. Which lamp is real takes a second pass to resolve, and the script does not have a second pass available.

rounds.notes: Approved. Weakest payoff of the approved set; if retention drops at 0:42 the ending is the reason.

reasons.hook: Eight words and a complete mystery. Joint best in the batch.
reasons.retention: Well paced, and the seasons time-lapse earns its place.
reasons.originality: Docked hard. A house that people enter and never leave is the most familiar territory anything in this database touches, and the script does nothing structural to make it feel new.
reasons.twist: Rejected. 'She has never been recorded leaving either' is the ending most of the audience will have guessed by 0:20 - the script spends twelve seconds arriving somewhere the viewer already is. A twist the viewer beats you to is not a twist.
reasons.visual: Doorbell fisheye is instantly readable but visually monotonous across ten scenes.

rounds.notes: Rejected on a predictable payoff. The hook is too good to waste - rewrite the reversal, keep the first eight words.

triggers.twist_predictable: reviewer: 'she has never been recorded leaving either' is the ending most of the audience will have guessed by 0:20. A twist the viewer beats you to is not a twist.

reasons.hook: Untouched by the rewrite, and still joint best in the batch.
reasons.retention: The slow-down sequence at 0:26 is a genuine investigation beat, which the original did not have - it replaced transit with discovery.
reasons.originality: Recovered. The script is no longer a house-that-keeps-people story; it is an identity story wearing that shape for the first twenty seconds, which is a far less worn position.
reasons.twist: Recovered but not full marks. 'All thirty-one are her' is a real reversal that very few viewers will predict from the opening, though the broader shape - the investigator is the subject - is itself familiar. The locked-door line is what makes it land.
reasons.visual: Unchanged. Doorbell fisheye across ten scenes is still visually monotonous; the overlaid-silhouettes shot helps.

rounds.notes: Approved. Visual monotony is the remaining weakness and is a shot-list problem, not a script problem.
rounds.rewrite_note: Replaced the predictable payoff. The original ended on 'she has never been recorded leaving either', which the audience reaches by 0:20. The rewrite keeps the hook and the first five lines intact and turns the reversal into identity: every one of the thirty-one arrivals is her. Five captions, five visuals and five prompts rewritten accordingly.
